usb.title: My controller is not in the list
usb.why: DJI controllers with a screen (such as the DJI RC 2 that comes with the Avata 360) do not show up as game controllers. Chrome can show what such a controller offers over USB: connect it with a data cable, switch it on, press the button below and choose it in Chrome's list.
usb.verdict.rc2: This controller sends its sticks on DJI's own channel. The simulator can try to read them straight from Chrome.
usb.rc2.claimFailed: Chrome could not open the controller's stick channel. On Windows this channel belongs to another driver (DJI Assistant 2 installs one), and Chrome can only open channels that use Windows' own USB driver. Nothing is broken: the controller and DJI's apps work as before, and nothing on them was changed. Fly with the keyboard, a gamepad or a radio for now, and press "Send this list" so we know your setup. On Linux, macOS or ChromeOS the same button may work, but that has not been tested yet.
usb.rc2.claimBridge: On Windows a small helper program for DJI controllers reads the sticks through DJI's own driver; the simulator tries it now.
usb.rc2.bridgeGet: How it works (its source on GitHub).
usb.rc2.helperNeeds: Save both files into one folder (Downloads is fine). The helper needs Python 3.8 or newer, which is free; if it is missing, the helper's window says how to get it. No administrator rights are needed.
usb.rc2.lost: The DJI controller stopped sending its sticks (unplugged, switched off or its helper program was closed), so the motors were stopped. Connect it again under Controls.
usb.rc2.silent: The controller is connected but did not send its sticks. Switch it on, wait until its screen has fully started and press the button again.
usb.rc2.bridgeWhy: Windows with DJI Assistant 2 installed: a small helper program for DJI controllers reads the sticks. Download its two files below, connect the controller with a data cable, switch it on, close DJI Assistant 2 and double-click start-dji-helper.cmd. If Chrome asks whether this site may reach apps on this device, allow it.
usb.rc2.bridgeAsk: Chrome is asking whether this site may reach apps on this device (a small window under the address bar). Press Allow: the simulator connects to the helper program as soon as you do.
usb.rc2.noBridge: The helper program does not answer. 1. Double-click start-dji-helper.cmd in the folder you downloaded. 2. Leave its window open. The simulator connects by itself as soon as it runs, or press "Fly with the helper program" again. If you blocked Chrome's question about apps on this device, allow it in the site settings (the icon left of the address).
usb.rc2.bridgeNoController: The helper program is running but does not see the controller. Connect it with a data cable, switch it on and close DJI Assistant 2; the simulator connects by itself.
usb.verdict.connect: It has a joystick part: close this and press "Radio or controller over USB (EdgeTX, DJI)".
usb.verdict.drone: This is the drone itself, not its controller. Connect the controller instead.
usb.verdict.none: Nothing here gives the sticks to a browser yet. Send this list and we will look at adding this controller.
usb.verdict.empty: Chrome sees the device but not its parts. Send this list and we will look into it.
usb.noApi: This browser cannot look at USB devices here. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
usb.nothingChosen: No device was chosen. If your controller is not in Chrome's list, check that it is switched on and that the cable carries data, not only charge.
usb.failed: Chrome could not read this device. Close DJI Assistant and DJI Fly on this computer and try again.
usb.report.head: My controller is not in the list: {name}. It offers:
usb.connect.hint: Plug the controller in with a data cable and switch it on, press the button and pick it in Chrome's list. A gamepad needs no button: move a stick. The setup then starts by itself.
usb.connect.again: Your controller was not in that list. Press the button once more: Chrome then shows DJI controllers that are not game controllers.
usb.connect.none: No controller was chosen. Check that it is switched on and that the cable carries data, not only charge, then press the button again.
usb.connect.noApi: This browser cannot open controllers over USB. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer, or move a stick of a gamepad.
usb.untested: {name} is a DJI controller this simulator has not been tested with yet. It is tried the same way as the DJI RC 2.
